hints: Integrate $a(4x-3)^{-2} + 2$ with respect to $x$ using the reverse chain rule to get $-\frac{a}{4(4x-3)} + 2x$.
Evaluate the antiderivative at the upper limit $x = 3$ and lower limit $x = 1$.
Subtract the lower limit from the upper limit, set the result equal to 12, and solve for $a$.
walkthrough:
Integrate term-by-term with respect to $x$ using the reverse chain rule:
$$\int \left(a(4x - 3)^{-2} + 2\right) dx = \left[ -\frac{a}{4}(4x - 3)^{-1} + 2x \right]_1^3 = \left[ -\frac{a}{4(4x - 3)} + 2x \right]_1^3$$

Evaluate the integrated expression at limits $x = 3$ and $x = 1$:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{At } x = 3: &\quad -\frac{a}{4(9)} + 2(3) = -\frac{a}{36} + 6 \\ \text{At } x = 1: &\quad -\frac{a}{4(1)} + 2(1) = -\frac{a}{4} + 2 \end{aligned}$$

Subtract the lower limit from the upper limit and equate to $12$:
$$\left(-\frac{a}{36} + 6\right) - \left(-\frac{a}{4} + 2\right) = 12 \implies \frac{8a}{36} + 4 = 12 \implies \frac{2a}{9} + 4 = 12$$

Solve the linear equation for constant $a$:
$$\frac{2a}{9} = 8 \implies 2a = 72 \implies a = 36$$
